title: `PERLLIB` is not set correctly.
body:
https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun/blob/b1ef744989533d8b1b4327b647fb315a42765ab9/src/main.rs#L719-L721

At least on archlinux, `/usr/lib/perl5` contains a subdirectory named `5.42`.

**And more importantly**, that splits into 3 directories:  

* `/usr/lib/perl5/5.42/core_perl`  
* `/usr/lib/perl5/5.42/site_perl` 
* `/usr/lib/perl5/5.42/vendor_perl`

Those 3 directories is what `PERLLIB` needs to point to in `SHARUN_DIR`, each entry being colon separated.

Also, there is additionl `perl` modules in: 

* `/usr/share/perl5/core_perl`  
* `/usr/share/perl5/site_perl` 
* `/usr/share/perl5/vendor_perl`

So the variable actually needs to include ALL of these 🫠

[I had to do this in the meantime.](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/GCstar-AppImage/blob/main/AppDir/bin/perl-pain.src.hook)

title: wrappe looks like it is unmaintained. Is it better to make universal AppImage?
body:
Thanks for an incredible tool! I am thinking of using it for the game Oolite which was recently published on FlatHub and the Windows Store. It is also available as an AppImage, but I've struggled with the old dependencies from building on Ubuntu 22.04.

I see your tool outputs a wrappe executable which looks like a great format, but I've also noticed there hasn't been any activity on the repo for a couple of years: https://github.com/Systemcluster/wrappe. I see your fork a few commits ahead. Are you planning to take over maintenance? If not, would it be better to focus on AppImage?

One thing that wrappe misses is an environment variable for the location of the original executable. As I understand it, there is WRAPPE_LAUNCH_DIR (inherited working directory similar to AppImage env var CWD) and WRAPPE_UNPACK_DIR (where the temporary extracted files are located, similar to env var APPDIR). If I launch my wrappe executable in folder A from another folder B, then WRAPPE_LAUNCH_DIR will be folder B. I need folder A to enable finding the game's user data (similar to finding the folder from the APPIMAGE env var). I was going to create an issue for this at Systemcluster/wrappe, but noticed the lack of activity there.

Please can you let me know what you know of the status of wrappe so I can decide whether to use it or go for a universal AppImage instead probably following these instructions: https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/blob/main/HOW-TO-MAKE-THESE.md.

title: sharun as the dynamic linker
body:
sometimes apps break becasue they read themselves, like examples: 

* https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/opencode-AppImage-Enhanced/blob/78699bad6189f9a4eb56140085166555f2c6fb4d/make-appimage.sh#L23-L32

* https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/wine-AppImage/blob/d595821125adbe3f56f4e4c74d13e08c5fc93715/make-appimage.sh#L44-L58

Would be great if we had the option to set sharun as the dynamic linker, the logic would be like this: 

* `lib4bin` would run `patchelf --set-interpreter /tmp/.sharun` instead of making hardlinks.

* The binary would be copied to `${SHARUN_DIR}/bin` instead of `${SHARUN-DIR}/shared/bin`

* When sharun is the `AppRun` it would copy itself to `/tmp/.sharun` before jumping to exec the binaries.

* Then when `/tmp/.sharun` is executed by the kernel, it would figure out where the dynamic linker is by checking `SHARUN_DIR` and do the rest of stuff it already does. 

---

I don't think we need to make this random, since sharun already is a static binary we can pick a fixed name, then sharun would be responsible for just make sure that `/tmp/.sharun` is present. 

It may also be possible to glue sharun into the binary itself, [polyfill glibc does this already](https://github.com/corsix/polyfill-glibc/blob/dd59051faaa10ee63c1b96f1b47bf9fcd3770ee2/src/x86_64/relative_interp_runtime.c), but it is likely this will break some binaries though.

ImageMagick is complicated.

It has a ton of config files all over the place in `/usr/share/ImageMagick` `/usr/lib/ImageMagick` and `/etc/ImageMagick`

It turns out you can put all those files in and a single directory and set `MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH` to it, tested it working and all fine here.

---

What is not complete is all the env variables that sharun would need to set, It is beyond my rust capabilities: 

* `MAGICK_HOME=$(SHARUN_DIR)` When imageMagick is compiled with a portable flag. We also need to set these others for when ImageMagick is not compiled portable:

* `MAGICK_CODER_FILTER_PATH=${SHARUN_DIR}/lib/ImageMagick*/modules*/filters`

* `MAGICK_CODER_MODULE_PATH=${SHARUN_DIR}/lib/ImageMagick*/modules*/coders`

* `MAGICK_CONFIGURE_PATH=${SHARUN_DIR}/etc/ImageMagick*`

[See what I'm doing in shell](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/blob/91aa9b3447ca775ab9a2ec4f11c8b171e854b7a3/useful-tools/quick-sharun.sh#L2080-L2105)

title: do not deploy dependencies for `libqgtk3.so`
body: This is the Qt plugin that allows Qt apps to follow the GTK theme of the host. The problem is that, it is highly likely that when an appimage is deployed, not all dependencies for `libqgtk3.so` are going to present, since that means gtk3, gio and gdk-pixbuf needs to be added to the container. * If all of gtk3 gets added to the application, nothing bad happens. * If none of gtk3 gets added, nothing bad happens either. * If **some** of the dependencies of `libqgtk3.so` get added, **then issues happen** See https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Dolphin-emu-AppImage/issues/41 This was caused because the gdkpixbuf that linked to glycin was added to the appimage, this caused the application to crash when you went to use the file picker. I fixed it by adding the gdk-pixbuf2 that doesn't depend on glycin, however a much better thing to do is just not deploy the dependencies of this at all. You can test this with the Qt6+dbus demo here: https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/releases/tag/demo If the host has no gtk at all, Qt just doesn't use this plugin as it will fail to load: And if the host has gtk installed, then Qt is able to use the plugin without issue, even if the host is alpine linux:

title: 3D-viewport can break in some applications (e.g. PrusaSlicer) after #66
body:
The issue is reproducible via:
Get a PrusaSlicer AppImage from [here](https://github.com/sarrchri/PrusaSlicer.AppImage/releases/tag/broken), that build uses the latest sharun.
Run the appimage on a system with e.g. Intel iGPU/AMD laptop iGPU and no external NVIDIA/AMD GPU, but that has nvidia drivers still installed.
You will see that the 3D print plate view is not working.

Then test the first [build on the repo](https://github.com/sarrchri/PrusaSlicer.AppImage/releases/2.9.4-1%402025-11-19_1763584326/), and you will notice everything works.

The only difference between those builds (aside from some dependencies being newer versions), is sharun having updated.
Me and @Samueru-sama have been troubleshooting this (also huge thanks! <3) and arrived at the conclusion that the fixes introduced with #66 are the cause.
Per their suggestion, I manually replaced the newer sharun (0.7.7) with the older one (0.7.4), linked the necessary files, ran AppRun, and observed that PrusaSlicer was then working no problem.

After that, also made sure linking the `10_nvidia.json` under `glvnd` folder structure, also did not break anything.

title: Issue hooking XKB on Arch Linux
body:
Heya. I'm trying to pack PrusaSlicer into an AppImage and switched to Arch Linux to make use of debloated llvm libs..
The packing failed because sharun hook for XKB tries to copy a singular file to in place of a folder.
I'm using Sharun v0.7.5

```
[ INFO ][2025.11.18 11:34:49]: [ STRIP ]: [/__w/prusaslicer-appimage/prusaslicer-appimage/PrusaSlicer/AppDir/shared/lib/libxkbcommon.so.0.13.0] 
[ INFO ][2025.11.18 11:34:49]: [ HOOK ]: copy X11 xkb... 
mkdir: created directory '/__w/prusaslicer-appimage/prusaslicer-appimage/PrusaSlicer/AppDir/share/X11'
mkdir: created directory '/__w/prusaslicer-appimage/prusaslicer-appimage/PrusaSlicer/AppDir/share/X11/xkb'
cp: cannot overwrite directory '/__w/prusaslicer-appimage/prusaslicer-appimage/PrusaSlicer/AppDir/share/X11/xkb' with non-directory '/usr/share/X11/xkb'
```

I took a look and it seems on Debian 12 and Ubuntu (at least Jammy and up) the package responsible for these files is `xkb-data` and on Arch Linux it is `xkeyboard-config`.
Arch Linux has the files under `/usr/share/xkeyboard-config-2/` and the file `/usr/share/X11/xkb` seems to be a symlink to the location `/usr/share/xkeyboard-config-2`, while Debian 12 (and Ubuntu) have all the files under `/usr/share/X11/xkb/`.

I could probably make the packing work by deleting the symlink on the container and copying the files to where the symlink was (and I might actually do it to get it done), but I thought I should report this anyway.

title: Nvidia driver will not work if `/usr/lib` contains libs of a different arch
body: Got a report at Eden that the AppImage was not able to detect the nvidia gpu in Aurora OS, the reason is this: * When the vulkan loader loads the nvidia driver, the dynamic linker then tries to find the dependencies of that driver. * Since the AppImage was on archlinux, the dynamic linker assumes that `/usr/lib` is where the 64bit libs are located. * But on other distros, that is instead in `/usr/lib64` and as result it attempt to load a 32bit dependency causing it to fail. --- In this specific case, setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib64` fixed the issue. I think the simplest solution is adding `/usr/lib64` to `--library-path` when we detect that `/usr/lib` contains non 64bit libraries.

title: add `xdg-open` wrapper
body:
One well known issue with env variables is that they propagate to child processes. 

So for example if something like `GDK_PIXBUF_MODULEDIR` is set to point to the bundled gdk in the AppImage, all applications launched by it will try to use it as well causing issues. 

We had this issue with [ghostty](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/ghostty-appimage/issues/36) already where we fixed it with some hacks using `ld-preload-open` but I just realized that we didn't have to do this.

Or this other issue with [QT_PLUGIN_PATH](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun/issues/8) which thankfully Qt provides a different method to fix this.

All that's needed is a wrapper script for `xdg-open` that unsets the env variables that point to libs bundled in the AppImage, and then launch `xdg-open`, something like this: 

```
#!/bin/sh
# xdg-open wrapper made by sharun, unsets env variables likely to cause issues

CURRENTDIR="$(readlink -f "$(dirname "$0")")"
PATH="$(echo "$PATH" | sed "s|$CURRENTDIR:||g")"
export PATH
unset BABL_PATH \
	GBM_BACKENDS_PATH \
	GCONV_PATH \
	GDK_PIXBUF_MODULEDIR \
	GDK_PIXBUF_MODULE_FILE \
	GEGL_PATH \
	GIO_MODULE_DIR \
	GI_TYPELIB_PATH \
	GSETTINGS_SCHEMA_DIR \
	GST_PLUGIN_PATH \
	GST_PLUGIN_SCANNER \
	GST_PLUGIN_SYSTEM_PATH \
	GST_PLUGIN_SYSTEM_PATH_1_0 \
	GTK_DATA_PREFIX \
	GTK_EXE_PREFIX \
	GTK_IM_MODULE_FILE \
	GTK_PATH \
	LIBDECOR_PLUGIN_DIR \
	LIBGL_DRIVERS_PATH \
	PERLLIB \
	PIPEWIRE_MODULE_DIR \
	QT_PLUGIN_PATH \
	SPA_PLUGIN_DIR \
	TCL_LIBRARY \
	TK_LIBRARY \
	XTABLES_LIBDIR

exec xdg-open "$@"
```

snap actually does something similar because they have this issue as well

title: [Feat] Add option to use the host glibc and dynamic linker on the fly
body:
One "issue" that AppImages made with sharun have is that we need to bundle our own mesa for hardware accelerated apps. 

And while it is possible to do this even while making them very small still, this has the downside that the AppImage needs to be kept up to date. 

Also there are cases where shipping mesa isn't really needed, like I do with mpv where I make the AppImage on archlinux and then expect the thing to just use the host mesa which works fine. But after a while mesa will stop working if not kept up to date.


Given that it is possible to directly just drop a newer glibc into the AppImage like I did [here](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/AppImageUpdate-Enhanced-Edition/blob/main/ci/build-appimages.sh#L78-L87) it is possible to also just make sharun do this on its own, the steps would be the following: 

* An env variable like `SHARUN_USE_HOST_GLIBC` would need to be set.

* `sharun` checks `/lib/libc.so.6 --version` and compares it to the version of the bundled `libc.so.6` This operation is also very fast and I checked with hyperfine and it takes 300 microseconds to get the version of libc.so.6

* If it is newer then sharun makes a temp dir in `/tmp` and symlinks the host `libc.so.6`, `ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` and `libpthread.so.0` to that directory. 

* finally sharun uses that `/tmp/$RANDOM/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2` as the dynamic linker **and adds that temp directory first to** `--library-path` so we can switch glibc at runtime without issues.

title: Add param to respect host's `lib´` dir structure (aka `multi-os-directory/multiarch`)
body:
### Description

As discussed in https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun/issues/17#issuecomment-2775118403, when sharun/lib4bin bundles some *.so file on DST_DIR, it will copy it on `lib/` dir in the ArchLinux fashion. However, Debian uses a different structure, for example: `lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/`. Fedora, on the other hand, uses `lib64/`.

Since the lib dir where the libraries are now is different from they were on host, this creates room to unexpected bugs not related to RPATH but to custom code of the libraries. While some bugs can be surpassed with hooks (after reported and triaged on this repo), other requires more study and invasive measures like editing *.so files (in libgimpbase case: https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun/issues/17#issuecomment-2770681879). 

### Feature

So, I would like, if it isn't being egoist, to have a param to respect host's lib dir structure and mantain it on DST_DIR. So, if a library is on /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/, it would be copied to DST_DIR/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/, and so on. 

### Use case

This would be useful to avoid unexpected bugs as explained above and very useful for debugging to by testing how the library behaves when it is where it should be. ~~Also, this would make sharun/lib4bin more consistent with the "praxis" of other appimage bundling tools~~

title: always unset `LD_PRELOAD`
body:
Is there an scenario where we should honor these variables at all? they are just going to cause missing symbol errors 90% of the time. 

We already had this issue with PrusaSlicer with one user having `LD_PRELOAD` set system wide causing a crash on the appimage as result, I fixed it by manually unsetting the variable but I think this just should be the default behaviour because I don't see a situation where these should be honored.

The change is propose is to always unset `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and `LD_PRELOAD` before sourcing the `.env` file, that way if the user user wants to still set the variables they can do it manually in the `.env`,

Another thing to look into is patch away the `/etc/ld.so.preload` path from the bundled dynamic linker to something like `/xxx/ld.so.preload` that way we avoid a similar issue but this time if the user has some library set in `/etc/ld.so.preload` [this was recently used by some malware](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/new-linux-backdoor-auto-color/) as well.

title: webkitgtk hook fails if multiple webkitgtk versions are installed
body:
Ref https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun/pull/5 (cc @Samueru-sama )

When users have more than one of webkitgtk 4.0, 4.1, and 6.0 installed, which is somewhat likely outside of CI envs, the script fails with
```
/home/fabianlars/.cache/tauri/lib4bin-x86_64: line 636: [: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/webkit2gtk-4.0: binary operator expected
```

Assuming that this error means that `sys_webkit_lib_dir` is not a single dir, imo it would be fine to simply include all of them considering the very small size of the files in question (but wouldn't mind if it could detect the version from the .so file or something).

I'm not _that_ familiar with bash scripts so i'm not very confident in fixing this myself but if nobody else has fixed (or closed it as wontfix) i'll try to take a stab at it anyway once my use case has gotten past the proof-of-concept stage.

title: Automatically handle all binaries in `shared/lib`
body:
Instead of doing what I did [here](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/sharun/blob/main/lib4bin#L640-L647) for webkit2gtk.

`lib4bin` should check all files in `lib` and if they are binaries then move them to `shared/bin` and put a relative symlink to sharun at their original location. 

It should be relative easy to do.

* Check all **elf** files in `shared/lib`.

* Make sure they are not static

* Make sure they don't contain `.so*` in their name since old distros have binaries that show as shared objects. 

* Move and symlink to sharun.
